newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Peptor to raise $30-35 mln in U.S. IPO.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Peptor to raise $30-35 mln in U.S. IPO.

text.p: Peptor Ltd, an Israeli developer of drugs, is expected to raise $30 million to $35 million this week in an initial public offering in New York, market sources said on Tuesday.

The offering, for which Peptor filed a prospectus on Friday, is for two million shares to be sold at $14 to $16 each and representing about 26 percent of equity. First Boston and Volpe Brown Whelan are the underwriters.
The shares will be traded on both Nasdaq and Easdaq, making Peptor the first Israeli company to trade on the new European quotation system.

Peptor develops SCAPL (small cyclical analogues of peptide loops) drugs. Peptide loops comprise the biologically active parts of proteins and peptides. Using advanced computer imaging and chemistry, Peptor finds the best molecular structure for a substance with therapeutic value.

The company has a $45 million joint venture with Israel's Teva Pharamceutical Industries to develop a treatment for autoimmune diseases such as rheumatoid arthritis. Teva also holds eight percent of Peptor.
Other companies collaborating with Peptor include Neoprobe Corp, Mallinckrodt, Xoma Corp and Ares-Serono Group.
